body:
## Summary

Research package connecting two bodies of work, per a scheduled research task:

- **Algorithmic economics / information elicitation**: proper scoring rules, prediction markets, and peer prediction, as studied by the [CU Boulder Algorithmic Economics group](https://www.colorado.edu/cs-theory/alg-econ), [Bo Waggoner](https://www.bowaggoner.com/), and [Rafael Frongillo](https://raf.prof/index.html).
- **Verifiable / decentralized ML training**, as studied by [Gensyn's research team](https://www.gensyn.ai/research) (Frongillo is concurrently Gensyn's Head of Research; researchers Gabriel Andrade, Oğuzhan Ersoy, and Marx Zang all work on this).

The concrete connecting idea: Gensyn's **Verde** verifies distributed training via expensive referee recomputation, and **Credibly Neutral AI Oracles** bounds manipulation of an independent report layer at `eps*(1-eps)`. This package asks whether **peer-prediction mechanisms** (Peer Truth Serum, Correlated Agreement — Waggoner/Frongillo's specialty) can replace most of that ground-truth recomputation while staying incentive-compatible, with an LMSR market maker (exploiting Gensyn's own "prediction markets are learning algorithms" equivalence) aggregating reports online into a calibrated correctness probability.

## What's included

- `scoring_rules.py`, `peer_prediction.py`, `market_maker.py`, `agents.py`, `simulation.py`, `metrics.py` — dependency-free Python implementation.
- 32 unit tests (pure `unittest`, no third-party deps).
- `experiments/run_experiment.py` — reproduces the results below.
- `README.md` — full research write-up, citations, and results table.

## Key result (also a documented limitation, not a hidden bug)

Peer Truth Serum stays incentive-compatible even under heavy simultaneous deviation (honest advantage +550 vs. best deviation). Correlated Agreement, implemented as a population-pooled delta matrix, does **not** — its incentive-compatibility theorem (Dasgupta & Ghosh 2013) is proven only for a single unilateral deviator, and a large colluding/lazy block can free-ride on honest-honest correlation under a skewed base rate. Both the vulnerability and the reason for it are explicitly tested (`test_ca_is_vulnerable_to_simultaneous_correlated_deviation`) and documented in the README's Limitations section, alongside the case where CA does hold (single deviator).

With a 5% audit fraction, 95% of simulated training steps never need full ground-truth recomputation; the LMSR market's price tracks ground truth with a Brier score of 0.02.

## Test plan

- [x] `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 32/32 passing
- [x] `python3 experiments/run_experiment.py` — reproduces the numbers quoted in the README
